attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post of 2024-06-05, written in his own voice. He is not quoting or paraphrasing anyone else.

semantics.note: The normalised wording keeps the 'I can't think of' qualifier, limits the scope to models that existed in 2024 when he wrote, and keeps the 'behind the curve' judgment. It adds no benchmark, threshold or deadline.

contract.note: The contract rightly treats the first sentence as a qualified recollection and 'behind the curve' as having no measurable target. Choosing benchmarks or a trajectory would add commitments he did not make. The not_applicable axis is fair to his words.

evidence.note: The speaker's own post, quoted accurately and correctly dated. It only establishes the wording and scope. It cannot prove his own claim and contains no independent data on model performance.

reviews.rationale: The first sentence reports what Marcus could recall on 2024-06-05, not a flat claim that no such measure exists, so benchmark results could not refute it. 'Behind the curve' is a judgment with no defined trajectory or target. The packet holds only his own post. The case is intact but untestable as written, so it is not adjudicable.
